metadata.research_goal: Synthesize swimming-specific strength and conditioning, injury risk, load monitoring, dryland support, mobility, equipment exposure, and return-to-swim rules into backend-ready planning records.
scope: neck symptoms from breathing and head position
low-back load in butterfly, breaststroke, streamlines, and underwaters
paddles, fins, pull buoy, kickboard, and snorkel modifiers
strength, mobility, trunk, hip, and ankle support
return-to-swim gates after shoulder, back, knee, groin, or long-break flags
excluded_scope: full stroke-teaching progressions except where mechanics change load
event programming except where load or return-to-swim gates depend on event
metadata.source_selection_note: Sources emphasize federation or official safety material, sports medicine reviews, peer-reviewed swimming injury/load studies, and reputable clinician-coaching education. The records synthesize and do not reproduce copyrighted programs.

key_concepts.name: Swimming removes ground impact but concentrates repetitive joint load
key_concepts.summary: Swimming is low impact for the lower limbs, but each practice can contain thousands of shoulder cycles plus repeated neck rotation, trunk extension, kicking, walls, and equipment-assisted repetitions.
key_concepts.backend_use: Do not reduce swim injury risk just because impact load is low; track repetition, stroke, equipment, and symptoms.

key_concepts.name: Load must be separated by stroke and anatomical channel
key_concepts.summary: Freestyle/backstroke emphasize shoulder, scapular, elbow, wrist, and neck exposure; butterfly and underwaters add trunk extension and high shoulder load; breaststroke adds medial knee, groin, and hip external-rotation load.
key_concepts.backend_use: Store stroke_volume fields rather than one generic yardage field.

key_concepts.name: Yardage is incomplete without internal response
key_concepts.summary: Distance, intensity, stroke mix, equipment, and dryland volume must be paired with RPE, pain location, next-day soreness, sleep, fatigue, and readiness because swimmers tolerate similar meters differently.
key_concepts.backend_use: Pair every swim_session_summary with external_load and internal_response fields.

key_concepts.name: Equipment is a load modifier, not a neutral accessory
key_concepts.summary: Paddles can increase shoulder and elbow stress, fins can change speed and kick demand, kickboards can alter shoulder and neck posture, and pull buoys shift work toward the upper body.
key_concepts.backend_use: Treat paddles, fins, kickboard, pull buoy, snorkel, cords, and tether work as exposure modifiers with contraindication rules.

key_concepts.name: Dryland should support water quality rather than drain it
key_concepts.summary: S&C is useful when it improves shoulder capacity, trunk control, hip function, starts, turns, and posture, but poorly placed upper-body fatigue can worsen technique and overload symptoms in the pool.
key_concepts.backend_use: Schedule dryland relative to key swims and automatically reduce upper-body dryland near high-intensity or high-paddle swim days.

key_concepts.name: Technique errors act like load multipliers
key_concepts.summary: Midline crossing, dropped elbow recovery/catch, poor body roll, thumb-down entry, excessive head lift, poor streamline, late butterfly timing, and knee-driven breaststroke kick can raise tissue stress without changing yardage.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use technique_flag fields to downgrade load readiness and prioritize drills before adding volume.

key_concepts.name: Return-to-swim has stages
key_concepts.summary: A swimmer can return to easy technical water exposure before returning to normal training and much later before returning to race-pace, paddles, butterfly, starts, or peak yardage.
key_concepts.backend_use: Represent return as staged gates: participation, training, sport, and performance rather than a single cleared boolean.

key_concepts.name: Breath control must never become unsafe breath holding
key_concepts.summary: Underwater skill and relaxed exhalation are relevant, but hyperventilation, extended breath holding, breath-hold games, and unsupervised underwater lap work create safety risk.
key_concepts.backend_use: Gate underwater and breath-control prescriptions by supervision, experience, pool context, and explicit no-hyperventilation rules.

key_concepts.name: Swimmer shoulder is not only rotator cuff strength
key_concepts.summary: Shoulder durability depends on rotator cuff capacity, serratus and scapular control, thoracic mobility, trunk control, breathing mechanics, stroke timing, and appropriate exposure.
key_concepts.backend_use: Bundle shoulder support records across cuff, scapula, thoracic, trunk, and technique rather than a single prehab drill.

key_concepts.name: Youth and masters swimmers need different risk gates
key_concepts.summary: Youth swimmers need age-appropriate development, growth-aware load progression, and supervision; masters swimmers may need more conservative return progression, mobility support, and recovery spacing.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use age_group and training_age fields when applying volume, dryland, equipment, and return-to-swim rules.

technical_models.name: Swimming load stack
technical_models.model: total_load = pool_distance + session_intensity + stroke_specific_volume + equipment_modifier + dryland_load + competition_load + internal_response
technical_models.use_case: Estimate recovery and injury-risk context without pretending yardage alone explains symptoms.

technical_models.name: Shoulder traffic light
technical_models.model: green = 0-2/10 pain that does not alter stroke and resolves by next day; yellow = 3-4/10, altered stroke, loss of range, or next-day soreness; red = sharp pain, night pain, weakness, neurological symptoms, or worsening trend.
technical_models.use_case: Control practice modification and referral prompts for swimmer shoulder.

technical_models.name: Breaststroke knee and groin gate
technical_models.model: breaststroke kick exposure progresses only if medial knee and adductor symptoms remain low, kick width is controlled, hip rotation supplies turnout, and next-day response is stable.
technical_models.use_case: Protect swimmers from adding breaststroke volume when knee or groin tissue is already reactive.

technical_models.name: Low-back extension load gate
technical_models.model: butterfly, dolphin kick, breaststroke pullout, aggressive streamline, and high-volume kick sets are limited when lumbar extension pain, repeated arching, or trunk fatigue is present.
technical_models.use_case: Modify stroke selection and dryland when low-back symptoms appear.

technical_models.name: Equipment exposure modifier
technical_models.model: equipment exposure changes tissue stress: paddles raise upper-limb resistance, pull buoy can concentrate shoulder work, fins increase speed and ankle/hip demand, kickboards can challenge shoulder/neck posture, and snorkels can reduce head-turning while requiring comfort.
technical_models.use_case: Generate safer substitutions when symptoms are present.

technical_models.name: Dryland placement model
technical_models.model: place high-load upper-body strength away from key swim quality, use low-fatigue activation before swim, reserve heavier strength for lower-priority swim days or after key water work, and avoid stacking paddles with heavy pulling.
technical_models.use_case: Coordinate dryland and pool training in generated weekly plans.

technical_models.name: Return-to-swim stages
technical_models.model: stage_0 = medical/rehab clearance and daily function; stage_1 = easy technique-only water; stage_2 = short aerobic intervals; stage_3 = normal stroke mix without equipment spikes; stage_4 = race pace, paddles, butterfly, starts, and competition exposure.
technical_models.use_case: Map injury history to safe session recommendations.

technical_models.name: Acute-to-chronic swimming guardrail
technical_models.model: compare the current week with recent chronic exposure for distance, session RPE load, high-intensity distance, and stroke-specific volume; flag sharp increases rather than using one universal safe threshold.
technical_models.use_case: Identify yardage spikes, sudden equipment changes, or stroke-specialization spikes before symptoms escalate.

technical_models.name: Underwater and breath-control safety gate
technical_models.model: underwater work requires demonstrated water competence, supervision, no hyperventilation, no extended breath holding, no breath-hold contests, conservative distances, and clear stop rules.
technical_models.use_case: Prevent unsafe hypoxic prescriptions in workouts.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not prescribe high-volume butterfly to beginners, swimmers with poor timing, or swimmers reporting extension-sensitive low-back symptoms.
tactical_rules.rationale: Butterfly adds shoulder load, repeated lumbar extension, and technique collapse risk when fatigue rises.

tactical_rules.rule: If shoulder, elbow, or wrist pain is present, remove paddles first and replace with short technical swimming, fins-assisted easy swimming, or non-aggravating kick work.
tactical_rules.rationale: Paddles amplify pulling resistance and can worsen symptoms when technique or tissue capacity is limited.

tactical_rules.rule: Avoid heavy upper-body pulling dryland on the same day or preceding day as high-paddle, high-pull, or race-pace upper-body swim sets.
tactical_rules.rationale: The combined fatigue can reduce catch quality and overload rotator cuff, scapular stabilizers, elbow, and wrist.

tactical_rules.rule: For medial knee or groin symptoms, first reduce breaststroke kick volume, kick intensity, and wide kick emphasis before reducing all swimming.
tactical_rules.rationale: Breaststroke-specific lower-limb mechanics can drive symptoms even when freestyle or backstroke remain tolerated.

tactical_rules.rule: When shoulder symptoms rise, prioritize hand-entry alignment, no midline crossing, body roll, relaxed recovery, and catch control before adding volume.
tactical_rules.rationale: Technique faults can multiply shoulder load independent of distance.

tactical_rules.rule: For neck irritation, reduce repeated one-sided breathing, head-lift breathing, and prolonged kickboard postures; use body roll, bilateral or controlled breathing, snorkel where appropriate, and arms-at-side kicking.
tactical_rules.rationale: Neck rotation/lift repeated hundreds of times can affect shoulder mechanics and cervical symptoms.

tactical_rules.rule: Flag any large increase in weekly distance, high-intensity distance, session count, or stroke-specific volume, especially if sleep, soreness, or pain trend worsens.
tactical_rules.rationale: Rapid load changes are more actionable than absolute yardage alone.

tactical_rules.rule: In return-to-swim sessions, stop or downshift when pain changes stroke mechanics, causes guarding, or worsens during the set.
tactical_rules.rationale: Altered mechanics can transfer load to other tissues and reinforce poor patterns.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not prescribe unsupervised hypoxic sets, extended breath holds, hyperventilation, or breath-hold contests.
tactical_rules.rationale: Hypoxic blackout risk is a safety issue, not a normal conditioning challenge.

tactical_rules.rule: Use fins to support body position or technique only when ankle, calf, hip, knee, and low-back response is acceptable; do not use long fin sets as default recovery.
tactical_rules.rationale: Fins can reduce shoulder strain in some contexts but increase speed, kick force, ankle demand, and lumbar extension exposure.

tactical_rules.rule: For youth swimmers returning from injury, progress volume, intensity, equipment, starts, and competition more conservatively and coordinate with coach/clinician/guardian context.
tactical_rules.rationale: Growth, training age, school load, and technique maturity influence risk.

tactical_rules.rule: Refer out or advise medical review for sharp pain, neurological symptoms, night pain, progressive weakness, persistent low-back pain in adolescent butterfly/breaststroke swimmers, or knee/groin pain that worsens despite load reduction.
tactical_rules.rationale: Some symptoms require diagnosis rather than app-level programming changes.

physical_demands.name: Shoulder rotator capacity
physical_demands.description: Repeated internal rotation, external rotation control, and overhead recovery require rotator cuff strength, endurance, and fatigue resistance.
train_with: progressive pulling strength away from key swim quality

physical_demands.name: Scapular upward rotation and protraction control
physical_demands.description: Serratus anterior, lower trapezius, and scapular control provide a stable base for repeated arm cycles.

physical_demands.name: Thoracic extension and rotation mobility
physical_demands.description: Thoracic mobility supports streamline, overhead reach, body roll, and shoulder mechanics without forcing excess lumbar extension.

physical_demands.name: Trunk anti-extension and body-line control
physical_demands.description: Streamline, kicking, butterfly, starts, and turns require the trunk to transmit force while limiting uncontrolled lumbar arching.

physical_demands.name: Hip rotation and adductor capacity
physical_demands.description: Breaststroke kick and turns require hip mobility, adductor capacity, and control so the knee does not absorb all turnout demand.
train_with: hip internal and external rotation mobility

physical_demands.name: Medial knee load tolerance
physical_demands.description: Breaststroke swimmers need tolerance to repetitive valgus/rotational knee stress, especially when kick width or volume increases.

physical_demands.name: Ankle plantar-flexion and kick comfort
physical_demands.description: Efficient flutter and dolphin kick need ankle mobility and plantar-flexion capacity; fins can increase demand if progressed too fast.

physical_demands.name: Start and turn power
physical_demands.description: Racing swimmers need lower-body power, trunk stiffness, landing and wall-skill coordination, and shoulder-safe streamline positions.

physical_demands.name: Aerobic base and recovery capacity
physical_demands.description: Even sprint swimmers need repeated high-quality practices; aerobic and recovery capacity help maintain stroke mechanics under training load.

physical_demands.name: Neck control and breathing mechanics
physical_demands.description: Freestyle and butterfly breathing can repeat cervical rotation or extension many times; head position should integrate with trunk roll and shoulder mechanics.
train_with: snorkel-assisted technique where safe and comfortable

injury_or_load_risks.name: Swimmer shoulder
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Shoulder pain may reflect multiple pathologies and often emerges from a combination of high repetition, fatigue, technique errors, mobility restrictions, scapular dysfunction, and load spikes.
warning_signs: cross-body entry or pull under fatigue

injury_or_load_risks.name: Supraspinatus tendon load from high swim volume
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: High weekly swimming workload has been linked with shoulder tendon risk in competitive swimmers, especially when volume and intensity outpace tissue capacity.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Scapular fatigue and dyskinesis
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Fatigue or weakness in serratus anterior, lower trapezius, and other scapular stabilizers can degrade shoulder mechanics across a long set.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Swimmer elbow
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Elbow tendon irritation can occur from repetitive pulling, backstroke/freestyle load, altered catch mechanics, and paddle-assisted stress.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Wrist irritation from entry, catch, or equipment
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Wrist pain is less emphasized than shoulder pain but can arise when hand entry, catch, paddle use, or wall contact overloads the wrist and forearm.
warning_signs: wrist extension pain after starts or walls

injury_or_load_risks.name: Neck irritation from breathing and head position
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Repeated one-sided head turn, head lift, poor body roll, and prolonged kickboard posture can irritate the neck and secondarily affect shoulder mechanics.
warning_signs: shoulder symptoms paired with neck stiffness

injury_or_load_risks.name: Low-back extension overload
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Butterfly, dolphin kick, breaststroke, pullouts, and aggressive streamline positions can repeatedly load lumbar extension, especially with weak trunk control or poor timing.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Adolescent low-back red flag
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Persistent or worsening low-back pain in adolescent butterfly or breaststroke swimmers should prompt clinical review because repeated hyperextension can be associated with spondylolysis.
warning_signs: declining tolerance to butterfly or breaststroke

injury_or_load_risks.name: Breaststroke knee
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Medial knee pain is strongly associated with breaststroke kick exposure and can be aggravated by wide, forceful, or knee-driven kick mechanics.
load_modifiers: turnout from knee rather than hip

injury_or_load_risks.name: Breaststroke groin and adductor load
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Breaststroke kick, turns, and wide or forceful hip positions can provoke adductor/groin symptoms when volume or intensity exceeds capacity.
warning_signs: pain during kick recovery or snap

injury_or_load_risks.name: Yardage spike
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: A sudden increase in total distance, session frequency, or weekly duration can exceed tissue adaptation even when intensity seems moderate.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Intensity spike
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Race-pace, sprint, lactate, power, starts, and resisted work can create high tendon and neuromuscular load even if total meters are low.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Paddle overuse
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Paddles can provide useful feedback and overload, but excessive or poorly timed paddle work can increase shoulder, elbow, and wrist stress.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Fin overuse
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Fins can help position and reduce some shoulder demand, but they can increase ankle, calf, hip, knee, and back loading through faster and stronger kicking.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Kickboard shoulder and neck posture
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Long kickboard sets can place the shoulders in sustained elevation or the neck in extension, which may not suit swimmers with shoulder or neck symptoms.

injury_or_load_risks.name: Hypoxic blackout risk
injury_or_load_risks.risk_summary: Extended breath holding, hyperventilation, underwater lap work, and breath-hold challenges can lead to loss of consciousness in water.

training_implications.summary: A swim plan should calculate total weekly stress from pool sessions, dryland strength, mobility, rehab/prehab, competitions, and cross-training rather than treating pool and gym as separate worlds.
training_implications.backend_action: Create a combined weekly load summary with pool and dryland subtotals.

training_implications.summary: Total distance should be broken down by freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, kick, pull, underwater, start, and turn exposure.
training_implications.backend_action: Add stroke_volume and skill_exposure fields to swim sessions.

training_implications.summary: Beginners with poor water confidence should receive breathing, floating, easy drills, and safe supervision rules before conditioning volume or underwater work.
training_implications.backend_action: Gate volume workouts behind water_confidence and safety assessment fields.

training_implications.summary: A long break should be handled like a load-readiness issue even without injury: short sessions, easy technique, no early paddles, and gradual frequency.
training_implications.backend_action: Trigger return_from_break progression when recent chronic swim load is low or absent.

training_implications.summary: Shoulder symptoms should shift the session toward technique, short rest-rich repeats, reduced pulling equipment, and lower total upper-limb stress.
training_implications.backend_action: Implement shoulder_pain modifications for workout generator.

training_implications.summary: Medial knee or groin symptoms should reduce breaststroke kick first while preserving tolerated freestyle/backstroke aerobic work if safe.
training_implications.backend_action: Add breaststroke_knee substitutions: pull-free easy freestyle, backstroke, vertical kick alternatives, or arms-only technique only if shoulder status permits.

training_implications.summary: Low-back symptoms should reduce butterfly, underwater dolphin kick, aggressive streamline volume, and high-volume breaststroke until trunk control and symptoms improve.
Equipment should have progression rules by size, distance, intensity, and symptom status; it should not appear automatically in every session.
training_implications.backend_action: Create equipment exposure budget and contraindication logic.

training_implications.summary: Mobility matters, but durable injury-risk support should include progressive strength and neuromuscular control rather than stretching-only prescriptions.
training_implications.backend_action: Create strength plus mobility templates for shoulder, trunk, hip, and ankle rather than standalone stretch routines.

training_implications.summary: Pre-swim dryland should be low-fatigue activation and mobility; strength or power that creates soreness belongs after key water work or on a planned dryland day.
A set can feel acceptable in the water but fail the next-day test; next-day shoulder, knee, groin, back, and fatigue response should control progression.
training_implications.backend_action: Collect next_day_response before progressing return-to-swim or equipment exposure.

training_implications.summary: Race pace, starts, turns, paddles, butterfly, high breaststroke kick volume, and competition should be reintroduced after easy and normal training are tolerated.
Most fitness swimmers and beginners do not need hypoxic sets; relaxed exhalation and normal breathing rhythm are safer and more relevant.
training_implications.backend_action: Suppress hypoxic workouts unless advanced swimmer, supervised context, and safe constraints are explicitly satisfied.

training_implications.summary: The legal underwater distance in racing should not be treated as a default training target, especially for fatigue, youth, beginners, or unsupervised swimmers.

backend_records_to_create.title: Swim Session Load Schema
backend_records_to_create.summary: Record pool distance, duration, RPE, stroke mix, equipment exposure, starts/turns, underwater work, dryland adjacency, and symptoms for every swim session.

backend_records_to_create.title: Stroke-Specific Load Counters
backend_records_to_create.summary: Separate freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, kick, pull, IM, open-water, and underwater exposure so load logic can match tissue risk.

backend_records_to_create.title: Shoulder Symptom Gate
backend_records_to_create.summary: Use pain score, altered mechanics, night pain, strength loss, and next-day response to choose normal, modified, deload, or referral output.

backend_records_to_create.title: Elbow and Wrist Symptom Gate
backend_records_to_create.summary: Track elbow, forearm, grip, and wrist symptoms and downshift paddle, sprint, and heavy grip dryland exposure when symptoms appear.

backend_records_to_create.title: Neck and Breathing Load Modifier
backend_records_to_create.summary: For neck symptoms, reduce one-sided breathing, head-lift breathing, and long kickboard sets while emphasizing body roll and relaxed exhalation.

backend_records_to_create.title: Low-Back Extension Gate
backend_records_to_create.summary: Limit butterfly, dolphin kick, breaststroke pullouts, and aggressive streamline exposure when extension-sensitive low-back symptoms are present.

backend_records_to_create.title: Adolescent Low-Back Referral Prompt
backend_records_to_create.summary: Prompt clinical review when adolescent swimmers report persistent or worsening low-back pain with butterfly, breaststroke, or extension.

backend_records_to_create.title: Breaststroke Knee Gate
backend_records_to_create.summary: Reduce breaststroke kick volume, intensity, and width when medial knee pain or next-day knee symptoms are present.

backend_records_to_create.title: Breaststroke Groin Gate
backend_records_to_create.summary: Monitor adductor and groin response to breaststroke kick and turns; progress adductor strength and reduce wide-forceful kick when symptoms occur.

backend_records_to_create.title: Yardage Spike Flag
backend_records_to_create.summary: Flag sudden increases in weekly swim distance or frequency, especially after low chronic load, travel, illness, or a training break.

backend_records_to_create.title: High-Intensity Swim Spike Flag
backend_records_to_create.summary: Flag sudden increases in sprint, race-pace, lactate, resisted, start, turn, or high-RPE work even when total distance is stable.

backend_records_to_create.title: Paddle Exposure Budget
backend_records_to_create.summary: Limit paddle distance by swimmer level, shoulder/elbow/wrist status, technique quality, paddle size, and recent paddle history.

backend_records_to_create.title: Fin Exposure Budget
backend_records_to_create.summary: Progress fin use by distance and intensity while monitoring ankle, calf, hip, knee, and low-back response.

backend_records_to_create.title: Kickboard Substitution Rule
backend_records_to_create.summary: Substitute arms-at-side kicking, snorkel-assisted kicking, or back kick when kickboard posture aggravates neck or shoulder symptoms.

backend_records_to_create.title: Pull Buoy Upper-Body Flag
backend_records_to_create.summary: Treat pull buoy distance as upper-body load and avoid using it as default recovery for shoulder, elbow, or wrist symptoms.

backend_records_to_create.title: Low-Fatigue Pre-Swim Activation
backend_records_to_create.summary: Use short activation and mobility before swim: scapular control, cuff activation, thoracic mobility, trunk bracing, hips, and ankles without fatigue.

backend_records_to_create.title: Dryland Strength Placement
backend_records_to_create.summary: Place heavier upper-body strength after key water work or away from quality swim sessions; avoid pre-fatiguing shoulders before important stroke work.

backend_records_to_create.title: Swimmer Shoulder Strength Template
backend_records_to_create.summary: Progress rotator cuff, serratus anterior, lower trapezius, rows, pressing tolerance, and trunk control while monitoring shoulder response.

backend_records_to_create.title: Thoracic and Streamline Mobility Template
backend_records_to_create.summary: Improve overhead streamline and body roll through thoracic extension/rotation and shoulder mobility while avoiding lumbar compensation.

backend_records_to_create.title: Trunk Anti-Extension and Rotation Control Template
backend_records_to_create.summary: Build trunk stiffness and control for streamlines, turns, starts, butterfly, and body-line maintenance.

backend_records_to_create.title: Breaststroke Hip and Adductor Support Template
backend_records_to_create.summary: Develop hip rotation control, adductor capacity, and knee-friendly lower-body strength for breaststroke swimmers.

backend_records_to_create.title: Ankle and Kick Mobility Template
backend_records_to_create.summary: Progress ankle plantar-flexion mobility, calf-foot capacity, and fin tolerance to support efficient flutter and dolphin kick.

backend_records_to_create.title: Return Stage 0: Clearance and Baseline Function
backend_records_to_create.summary: Before water return, confirm medical/rehab clearance where relevant, daily function tolerance, no red flags, basic range, and acceptable pain response.

backend_records_to_create.title: Return Stage 1: Technique-Only Water
backend_records_to_create.summary: Begin with low-volume, rest-rich, pain-gated drills and easy swimming, excluding paddles, sprinting, butterfly, high breaststroke kick, and hard underwaters.

backend_records_to_create.title: Return Stage 2: Short Aerobic Intervals
backend_records_to_create.summary: Progress to short easy intervals with controlled technique and modest volume increases only when current and next-day symptoms remain stable.

backend_records_to_create.title: Return Stage 3: Normal Training Rebuild
backend_records_to_create.summary: Rebuild normal training structure before race pace, large paddle sets, high butterfly, or high breaststroke kick; continue stroke-specific symptom checks.

backend_records_to_create.title: Return Stage 4: Performance Reintroduction
backend_records_to_create.summary: Reintroduce race pace, starts, turns, underwaters, paddles, butterfly, high breaststroke kick, and competition in small doses after normal training is tolerated.

backend_records_to_create.title: Return From Long Break Progression
backend_records_to_create.summary: When chronic swim exposure is low, restart with easy technique volume, conservative frequency, no early paddles, and next-day symptom gates even without a diagnosed injury.

backend_records_to_create.title: Underwater Safety Gate
backend_records_to_create.summary: Block extended breath holding, hyperventilation, breath-hold games, and unsupervised underwater lap work; allow only conservative supervised skill work for competent swimmers.

backend_records_to_create.title: Beginner Swim Safety Gate
backend_records_to_create.summary: Require comfort, face immersion, exhalation, floating/recovery, and safe pool context before assigning fitness volume or challenging intervals.

backend_records_to_create.title: Technique Load Flags
backend_records_to_create.summary: Flag midline crossing, thumb-down entry, dropped elbow, poor body roll, head lift, excessive lumbar arch, wide breaststroke kick, and fatigue technique collapse.

backend_records_to_create.title: Shoulder-Friendly Technique Substitution
backend_records_to_create.summary: Replace painful pull volume with short drill repeats, easy kicking that does not aggravate neck/shoulder, relaxed freestyle/backstroke technique, or non-water recovery depending on symptoms.

backend_records_to_create.title: Breaststroke Knee/Groin Substitution
backend_records_to_create.summary: Replace aggravating breaststroke kick with tolerated freestyle/backstroke aerobic work, gentle technique, or isolated hip/adductor rehab support.

backend_records_to_create.title: Low-Back Sensitive Swim Substitution
backend_records_to_create.summary: Replace butterfly, hard dolphin kick, and extension-heavy breaststroke with tolerated freestyle/backstroke technique and trunk-control dryland.

backend_records_to_create.title: Masters Recovery Modifier
backend_records_to_create.summary: For masters swimmers, apply conservative progression after breaks, monitor shoulder history, and separate hard pool and heavy dryland stress unless recovery is proven.

backend_records_to_create.title: Youth Growth and Training-Age Modifier
backend_records_to_create.summary: For youth swimmers, adjust volume, dryland intensity, breaststroke kick, and return progression by growth, training age, skill quality, and coach supervision.

backend_records_to_create.title: Next-Day Response Check-In
backend_records_to_create.summary: Ask for next-day shoulder, elbow, wrist, neck, back, knee, groin, sleep, soreness, and fatigue after hard, new, equipment-heavy, or return-to-swim sessions.

backend_records_to_create.title: Swimming Medical Review Red Flags
backend_records_to_create.summary: Prompt medical review for neurological symptoms, sharp acute pain, night pain, progressive weakness, persistent adolescent back pain, swelling/catching knee symptoms, or worsening symptoms despite deload.

backend_records_to_create.title: Open-Water and Triathlon Load Context
backend_records_to_create.summary: Track sighting, wetsuit context, continuous duration, anxiety, bilateral breathing comfort, and neck/shoulder response for open-water or triathlon swimmers.

backend_records_to_create.title: Start and Turn Power Integration
backend_records_to_create.summary: For racing swimmers, progress lower-body power, trunk stiffness, and streamline positions while coordinating with start/turn pool exposure and shoulder/back readiness.

backend_records_to_create.title: Swimming Load Monitoring Dashboard
backend_records_to_create.summary: Show weekly distance, session load, high-intensity distance, stroke mix, equipment exposure, dryland load, symptoms, and next-day response trends.

backend_records_to_create.title: No Blind Copy of Elite Yardage
backend_records_to_create.summary: Avoid copying elite or team yardage templates into user plans without swimmer level, chronic load, technique quality, pool access, recovery, and symptom context.
